newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends lower on bearish export news.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends lower on bearish export news.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed lower, with selling throughout the session largely motivated by a report Tuesday that 1997 Canadian lumber exports to the U.S. may match 1996's record amount of 17.8 million board feet despite an import quota, analysts said.
The report may have been a factor in Tuesday's sharply lower close, but continued to prompt selling Wednesday, traders said.

"Obviously the quota has not restricted anything. That's primarily becuase of the U.S. timber supply. They simply can't supply their own needs," said Doug Smyth, research director for the IWA-Canada union and author of the report.
Also, talk circulated in the CME market that Canada may be modifying lumber so that it can be shipped to the U.S. without being applied against the export quota, said one analyst
CME lumber closed down $8.60 to $0.50 per thousand board feet with July off the most at $374.00 per tbf.
